title: Evidence, Confidence, and Unknowns in Binary Analysis

questions.question: rea gives every Evidence record a confidence value. Which set of values does the schema allow?
options: A number from 0.0 to 1.0
observed, derived, or inferred
pass, fail, or unknown
low, medium, high, or critical
questions.explanation: Confidence is a three-value enum in src/domain/evidence.ts. Severity and completion statuses are different fields with their own values.

questions.question: Two people run the same rea query on the same object file in different folders on different machines. What happens to evidence_id?
options: It differs because the local path differs
It is the same because the hash excludes name and local_path
It is the same only when the folder names match
It differs because the machine clock differs
questions.explanation: The semantic projection keeps the subject digest, format, and architecture and drops name and local_path. The same observation of the same bytes gets the same id anywhere.

questions.question: A claim says grade(55) == 0. The ledger holds the Ghidra pseudocode record and the derived table model. What is the claim's status?
options: pass, because the pseudocode record is observed
pass, because two records agree with the claim
fail, because the pseudocode shows a different expression
unsupported, because no observed run states the result
questions.explanation: The pseudocode is an observation of what Ghidra printed, not of what the function returns. Only an observed run of the function can promote a behaviour claim.

questions.question: A snapshot was saved under profile digest a04af771. A later rea release changes jump_table_evidence to a v2 contract. What does the cache do with the snapshot?
options: Starts Ghidra and overwrites the old entries
Replays the entries and marks each one stale
Refuses the import with profile_mismatch
Replays only the entries that have no jump table
questions.explanation: The profile digest covers every contract version string. A changed version gives a new digest, and the snapshot no longer matches the active binding.

questions.question: What closes a residual unknown with the disposition verified?
options: At least one evidence id with the required confidence and authority
Removing the unknown from the ledger
A rationale sentence written by the analyst
A new revision with status resolved and an empty evidence list
questions.explanation: A verified resolution names evidence ids, and the ledger checks that each one is observed and carries the authority the unknown asked for.

questions.question: Runs of the host build showed grade(95) == 4 and grade(100) == 4. The claim covers every score from 90 to 100. Which status is correct?
options: unknown, because 2 of 11 inputs have observed runs
pass, because every observed run agreed with the claim
unsupported, because the x86-64 object itself never ran
fail, because nine inputs were never run
questions.explanation: Partial coverage is unknown, not pass and not fail. The unknown record stays open until the other nine inputs have observed runs.
